## Action required

Run `specflow upgrade` in every repo that has specflow installed. That is the entire release. It is
also the first release that can actually deliver a fix to those files, so an install that has been
upgrading since v0.1.0 is still running v0.1.0's copies until this runs.

```
specflow upgrade
specflow status     # `stale` should read `none` afterwards
```

## What was broken

`MANAGED` covered only files with a `specflow:start`/`specflow:end` region. The **adapters** — the
four Claude `SKILL.md` stubs and `.claude/hooks/specflow-handoff-reminder.sh` — are wholly generated
and carry no markers, so they sat outside it and were **create-once**: `upgrade` wrote one only when
it was absent. A corrected stub or hook never reached a repo that already had the file.

Concretely: v0.1.5 shipped `specflow next` / `claim` / `finish` into the procedures, but every
existing install's `finish-batch` skill still said to hand-edit `CLAIMS.md` and `BUILD_QUEUE.md`. A
skill is what an agent loads *before* the procedure, so that summary is what got acted on.

## What `upgrade` does to your tree

Per adapter file, in this order:

| On-disk state | Action |
|---|---|
| identical to the shipped version | baseline recorded, file untouched |
| matches its recorded baseline | replaced |
| no baseline (any install made before v0.1.6) | copied to `<file>.specflow-bak`, then replaced |
| differs from a baseline it has (you edited it) | **untouched**; new version written to `<file>.specflow-new` |

Every install predating v0.1.6 hits row 3 for any adapter it does not already match, so expect up to
five `.specflow-bak` files, named in the `upgrade` output. Delete them once you have looked; in a git
repo the originals are in history regardless. This is one-time — after this upgrade the files carry
baselines and follow rows 1, 2, and 4.

`AGENTS.md`, the procedures, your agent instruction files, `spec/`, `BUILD_QUEUE.md`, and `CLAIMS.md`
are unaffected by this change. `upgrade` still never commits.

## Behavior changes

- **`specflow status` gained a `stale` row.** `drift` now means *you* edited a managed file, so
  `upgrade` will not touch it. `stale` means *specflow* moved and the file did not, so `upgrade`
  will refresh it. Previously a version stamp matching the binary printed `drift: none` and read as
  "current" while a skill stub was several versions behind.
- **`specflow verify` covers the adapters.** A deleted, truncated, or hand-mangled `SKILL.md` or hook
  used to pass clean; it is now reported (missing and drifted are warnings, a spec-only mode leak is
  a problem). Fresh installs list all five under `✓`.
- **The four skill stubs name their verb.** `claim-batch` → `specflow next` / `specflow claim`;
  `finish-batch` → `specflow finish <N> --commit <sha> --summary-file <p> --done-file <p>`;
  `prune-ledgers` → notes that `specflow finish` already does the `CLAIMS.md` half. The `spec-edit`
  addition is `full-only`-gated, so a spec-only install still names no queue machinery.

## Fixes

- `normalizePath` trimmed a leading `.` along with trailing prose punctuation, so `.claude/…`,
  `.github/…`, and `.cursor/…` in a batch's `### Files this batch creates/edits` list compared as a
  different path. Every dotfile path was invisible to `specflow next`'s file-overlap check.

## Install

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MatanKoby/specflow/main/install.sh | sh
# or
go install github.com/MatanKoby/specflow/cmd/specflow@v0.1.6
```
